extracted_fields.objective: To conduct a decadal spatio-temporal analysis of Land Use Land Cover (LULC) changes in Taiwan from 1990 to 2020, and simulate future LULC for 2030 and 2050 using machine learning (Support Vector Machine) combined with Markov chain models under multiple scenarios incorporating environmental variables.
extracted_fields.land_use_classes: Built-up; Barren; Water Deep; Water Shallow; Uncultivated; Cultivated; Forest
extracted_fields.predictors: Aspect; Elevation; Hillshade; Distance to river; Distance to road; Slope
extracted_fields.population_selected: Yes; Taiwan’s demographic shifts including negative population growth rate considered in interpreting urbanization and LULC patterns, though not directly used as spatial predictor variables
extracted_fields.validation_data_sources:
Ground Control Points (655 GCPs for classification accuracy; 300 GCPs for predicted 2020 validation);
Actual classified LULC maps from Landsat images
extracted_fields.scalability: Yes; methodology and integrated SVM-Markov approach applicable to other rapidly urbanizing mid-sized economies and regions with diverse land uses and complex socio-ecological contexts
